_README: Zones for the island, cloned from a vanilla MTAreaVolume.
A zone is what makes people exist. MTZoneState is keyed by ZoneKey and
carries Server_Residents, NumResidents and BusTransportRate. Jeju ships
exactly seven volumes and Arini was inside none of them, so its bus stops
held 0 passengers no matter how long anyone waited.
world   = centre of the volume, WORLD coordinates.
scale   = RelativeScale3D on the brush, which is a unit box. This is the
volume the game tests against. Vanilla Gangjung uses
outline = HALF extent in uu of the rectangle drawn on the map. This is a
SEPARATE thing from the volume: TopViewLines is its own
world-space polygon, which is why a cloned zone kept drawing
Gangjung's shape over Arini no matter where the box went. Keep
it roughly consistent with scale by hand -- the relationship
between brush scale and world size has not been measured.
The zone registers and Arini appears in the resident system, but reports
0 residents. Residents likely need POIs to live at: MTResidentZoneState
carries a POIs array and MTZoneState a Server_Supermarkets one.
color = ZoneColor as [r, g, b, a], 0..1. Cloned from Gangjung it drew in
Gangjung's colour, which is the one thing that must not happen
when the point is telling two zones apart.
The square is built from the injected map's own extents: the larger of the
two mesh spans becomes the side, so it is square rather than merely
rectangular. Its EAST edge is pinned to X -457,000, which is where Jeju's
westernmost zones end -- Hallim at -458,080 and Gangjung at -456,942 -- so
Arini abuts both instead of floating in the sea with a gap.

THE FILL IS NOT OURS TO PLACE. A zone's UModel stores WORLD-SPACE
geometry -- Gangjung's model literally contains -456,942, which is that
zone's own TopViewLines minimum. Cloning it copies Gangjung's shape AND
its position, and our transform then scales that 7,212x. The border comes
from TopViewLines and is ours; the fill comes from the brush and is
Gangjung's, which is why it appears somewhere else entirely in a shape we
never authored.
Two consequences worth stating plainly:
1. The real containment volume is NOT the square drawn on the map. It
works only because 7,212x makes it big enough to swallow the island.
2. Fixing it properly means authoring BSP geometry, not setting a
2. Alpha 0 removed OUR border and label and left the stray fill untouched,
which means that fill is not drawn with our ZoneColor and is not ours.
OUTLINE ONLY, deliberately. The square drawn on the map is TopViewLines;
what the game tests against is the brush, and they are independent. This
build shrinks and moves the OUTLINE to clear Gapa and leaves `scale`
alone, so if residents change we learn something unexpected, and if the
fill changes we know it tracks the outline.
A 1.5x shrink on the same centre would still have overlapped Gapa by
284,000 x 393,000 uu, so it could not have tested the collision idea.
Pushed west instead: east edge at -1,000,000, clear of Gapa's -981,345.
Cost is 20 of 34 delivery points inside the drawn square, down from 34.
WORLD-SPACE geometry -- Gangjung's own outline minimum, -456,942, is in
those bytes. Scaling it 7,212x pushed the footprint to +/- 3 BILLION uu,
which is why colour covered the whole map while our border stayed correct:
the border comes from TopViewLines and is ours, the fill comes from the
brush and was Gangjung's, multiplied into nonsense.
CALIBRATION. The fill is the BRUSH, proven by scale: 7,212 drowned the
whole map in colour, 1 made the fill vanish entirely. Nothing about the
outline ever moved it -- not winding, not position, not clearing Gapa.
Z must stay large. At scale [1,1,1] the volume was also one unit TALL, a
paper-thin sheet at Z 46,440 that intersects nothing, so that build could
not distinguish 'too small' from 'too flat'.
4808 assumes the model is the +/-100 local box its float data suggests, so
side = scale * 200 = 961,600, matching the drawn outline. If the fill comes
back the same size as the border, that assumption is right and border,
fill and volume finally agree.
SOURCE IS NOBONG LANDFILL, not a zone. Its brush is a true 200-unit box --
50,000 world / scale 250 = 200, 40,000 / 200 = 200, exactly. Gangjung's is
a polygon, which is why the fill was never square no matter how it was
scaled or moved.
So: world size = scale * 200, and scale 4808 gives 961,600 uu -- the drawn
outline is 961,621. Border, fill and volume should finally be the same
square.
The source has no AreaVolumeFlags and no AreaName (it uses AreaNameTexts),
so the clone creates both: Zone, and an empty AreaName for the label to be
written into.
world MUST be the outline's centre. Moving the outline west to clear Gapa
without moving the volume left them 302,594 uu apart in X -- a quarter of
the width, which is exactly what the offset fill looked like. Y was never
wrong, because Y never moved.
Marker-authored zones derive both from the same corners and cannot drift
like this; it is only hand-edited outline_points that can.
